result.process_description:
Consider a process for purchasing items from an online shop.
The user starts an order by logging in to their account.
Then, the user simultaneously selects the items to purchase and sets a payment method.
Afterward, the user either pays or completes an installment agreement.
After selecting the items, the user chooses between multiple options for a free reward.
Since the reward value depends on the purchase value, this step is done after selecting the items, but it is independent of the payment activities.
Finally, the items are delivered.
The user has the right to return items for exchange.
Every time items are returned, a new delivery is made.

args.text: When a process description says activities happen simultaneously, or says one activity is independent of another while sharing a prerequisite, model their concurrency and dependencies with parallel gateways: split after the shared prerequisite, start each independent branch, and join branches that must both finish before continuing.

trace.reason: Check whether documented guidance already covers modeling simultaneous and independent activities with parallel gateways.

result.rule: Several unconditional outgoing flows from one activity can all proceed. Use a gateway when the description requires a decision or synchronization.
Use a parallel split when all outgoing branches start. Do not add decision conditions to parallel branches.
Do not merge separately described actions into one task or split one stated action without a process reason. Preserve described dependencies.
Use lanes to partition one process by a stated role, department, system or responsibility; lanes are not separate processes.
Sequence flows may cross lanes in one process. Use message flows across participant pools, never between lanes.
Use a parallel join when a shared continuation waits for all active parallel branches. Never use it to join mutually exclusive alternatives.

result.rule: When the description lays out activities in an order, or requires several activities to finish before a later stage or process end.: Connect the activities with sequence flows that preserve the stated order; when every required activity must finish before proceeding, synchronize their paths with a parallel gateway.

When the description names multiple required activities that must be completed before a later activity, without specifying an order among them: Model the activities as separate parallel branches and synchronize them before the later activity.

When the description says that distinct activities happen independently during the same ongoing period: Model the activities as separate branches from a parallel gateway rather than sequencing them, and synchronize the branches only if all must finish before the process continues.

When the description says an activity may or may not occur before the process continues: Model mutually exclusive paths for performing or skipping the activity, then merge the paths before the next step.
